subject: Finalize pricing schedule, net terms & tax treatment for Order Form
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Order Form – pricing schedule and invoicing questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is excited about moving this forward. Procurement ran the draft Order Form past Finance and Legal and we have a few commercial points we need clarified before we can finish internal approvals: 

1) Pricing schedule: Finance would like the line-item layout for the committed units by quarter and the proposed proration approach if we activate mid-quarter. Can you provide the XLS with the quarterly split?
2) Minimum commit: Acme needs confirmation on ramp flexibility — can we split the annual commit into three tranches with ability to reallocate within the first 90 days?
3) Net terms & invoice path: They require Net-45 to the billing entity Acme Cloud US, and a PO to be included on the invoice. We need to confirm Redwood’s billing entity for this deal and whether Net-45 is possible.
4) Taxes: Tom asked whether Redwood will add VAT/GST or if Acme will self-assess. We also need a W-9 or equivalent tax residency evidence to route payments.

We attached the internal PO template (see attachments@acme-corp.com). Please loop in Sales/Legal and let us know a short timeline — Procurement is targeting a signature by Sep 24.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Liu | Head of Procurement | Acme Corporation
attachments: PO_Acme_8742.pdf (pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood Order Form – pricing schedule and invoicing questions

Karthik / Kim — forwarding Acme’s asks below. High level: pricing schedule XLS is attached (we already shared v2, I’ve built a quarterly tranche view in Pricing_Schedule_20270917.xlsx).

Can Legal confirm:
- Is splitting the annual commit into three tranches (with internal reallocation flexibility for the first 90 days) acceptable from a risk perspective? If not, what guardrails would Legal require (e.g., minimums per tranche, notice windows)?
- Net-45 to Acme Cloud US: do we have any entity/AR constraints? Markus, help on entity/evidence.
- Tax treatment: do we want to require Acme to self-assess VAT (they’re in the U.S. but the entity is US-based) or do we list Redwood as charging tax where applicable?

Timeline: Dana wants signature by Sep 24. If Legal can do a short review with redlines by Mon 20th, Sales can negotiate the payment cadence.

I’m attaching the pricing XLS.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi | Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachments: Pricing_Schedule_20270917.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood Order Form – pricing schedule and invoicing questions

Irene / team — quick notes from Sales side after reviewing Acme’s asks: 

- Pricing XLS looks good; we can offer the quarterly split with proration on activation (standard = prorate by day within the quarter).
- For minimum commit flexibility, Sales prefers the 3-tranche split rather than a hard annual lock if Legal signs off on: 1) a combined minimum equal to 70% of the annual commit over the first 180 days, and 2) a reallocation right limited to within the first 90 days only. That preserves revenue predictability.
- Net-45: we historically bill Net-30 for self-serve, but enterprise deals can be Net-45 with approval. Need Finance confirmation on AR entity.

Kimberly — can Legal draft a short addendum to the Order Form that implements the tranche structure above and a proration clause? Markus, can you confirm which Redwood entity & tax docs we should provide to Acme?

If Legal can produce redlines by EOD Tue (21st) I’ll be ready to negotiate on Wed with Acme.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form – pricing schedule and invoicing questions

Dana / Irene — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a PDF with marked redlines (Redlines_Acme_v1.pdf) that: 

- Adds a 3-tranche schedule to the Order Form with a reallocation window (first 90 days) and a combined 70% minimum in the first 180 days.
- Inserts standard proration language (pro rata by day in quarter for mid-quarter activation).
- Proposes Net-45 to Acme Cloud US on the condition of a PO being included on invoices; Finance must approve the Net-45 exception.
- Adds a clause on taxes: Redwood will charge sales tax/VAT where required by law; where not required, Acme may self-assess. We will provide our W-9 and tax residency letter.

Open items we’d like Acme to confirm: 
- Which billing entity on the PO (Acme provided a PO template but did not state billing entity explicitly).
- Whether Acme’s Accounts Payable can accept electronic invoices with PO number in the invoice body (preferred) or require paper copies.

Attachments: Redlines_Acme_v1.pdf (pdf)

If these redlines are acceptable, we can push a DocuSign package with Order Form v3 and the pricing XLS. Karthik, I left 1 clause for commercial to weigh in (minimum % / timeline) — flagged in the PDF.

Best,
Kimberly Park | Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form – pricing schedule and invoicing questions

Kimberly / Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed Redlines_Acme_v1.pdf with Acme Finance and Legal: 

- The tranche / 70% combined minimum proposal is acceptable to Acme Finance provided the PO shows the billing entity as Acme Cloud US. I’ve attached a short note from Tom confirming the required billing entity and he’s copied.
- Acme Legal requests one minor change to the tax clause: they’d prefer explicit language allowing Acme to self-assess VAT where local law permits. I’ve attached their requested edit as a brief markup (see attachments).
- Net-45 is approved by Finance once Redwood confirms entity and attaches W-9/tax letter to the DocuSign package.

Next step: can Redwood (1) confirm which billing entity will appear on the invoice, (2) include Redwood’s W-9/tax residency letter in the DocuSign submission, and (3) issue the DocuSign by EOD Wed 22nd so we can hit our internal Sep 24 signature target?

We’re good to proceed pending those items.

Thanks,
Dana
attachments: Acme_PO_Template_filled.pdf (pdf), Acme_tax_edit_markup.pdf (pdf)
